This video explains a potential consequence of minimum wage laws.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IFbYM2EDz40

Now, straight away I know that many socialists will call the capitalist pig to slaughter, but those sort of people do not belong here and I don't really care about them.

In many countries, such as Australia, there is a national minimum wage law. That means, no matter what state you are in, you have the same minimum wage. In the USA, a fragmented minimum wage law only makes things worse for people. A key point that this video doesn't discuss, is that you can have one state next to another where the minimum wage law is almost double than the next. This is not a scaleable economy. There are many examples in the news this year of businesses getting up and moving out because it is unsustainable. If you have a product that cost $10 in one state and $10 dollars in another to create, then you have balanced economies. The moment a massive minimum wage law is introduced into one state, and its product now costs $15 to create, you can not sell this product anywhere, as people will just buy from the state next to them. Governments that do these sort of changes are ones not to do business in. No matter how sustainable you want to be, if the people in charge of the business law are not educated you will not get far without digging a hole and hiding (many businesses have to do this, or do it because they are greedy (tax evasion)).

Now many places have a low minimum wage. Many people consider these countries to consider their people worthless. China is a good example. If you take into consideration the cost of living and food there, you start to see that their low minimum wages are not so bad. Yes yes, I know China is a horrible country and their general standards of living compared to western worlds is atrocious, but if you stop for a moment and consider how they seem to survive like that so easily, you may re consider. They do not indulge in the useless luxury that western societies do. If you strip off every single thing you do not need in order to survive, such as your car, your fancy clothes, your phone, your computer, your TV, any meal that is not a piece of fish and rice or anything that you do not need in the event you end up living on the streets... Their cost of living is comparable.

The video covers the important business ideology of "each person must make money or they are not profitable". And if they are not profitable, why hire them? There are two business ideas that we should take to this regard.

If we all make money, then the business is happy.

If you build a business to a level that sustains itself and you are able to draw out a comfortable pay and you are able to pay your workers comfortably, you have made a self sustaining socialist utopia, out of capitalism. Every business I have started or looked at starting always pays minimum wage at the start. You just can not predict how much money you can safely give them. In my cases I don't actually pay myself out of the businesses I am the sole owner of as they are still in a growth phase. The extra money made goes into the business to make sure it grows and gets bigger so I can start taking money out. Once the business gets bigger I can start to increase the money my employees earn. This makes them happier and creates loyalty. Once you get to a happy size, you are free to distribute additional profits amongst the rest of your employees and the utopia is born. For those who have such imposing minimum wage laws amongst non imposing, you can not create this utopia.

I want to make all the money, but I am able to make my workers happy.

In some cases, you may wish to withdraw as much money as possible from business. Doing so though, does keep your workers at minimum wage. Reasons such as trying to build the business or trying to fund other projects may be the cause. As long as the reason is not "Because I am a greedy capitalist", then you might be able to be forgiven for all your workers being paid minimum wage. But you still must make their work environment and lives as easy and as pleasant as possible. Things like being nice, not being an asshole, being polite and not burning puppies aside, there are many cheap things you can do to make their lives better. Most people in the lower levels of society love free food. Imagine if they got a free lunch every day. A basic expense to most, but to a business it is a running cost and is deductible. You do not need to hire a catering company or a chef for this. A simple set of food available to all at any time of day is usually enough. For example, a fully stocked fruit bowl, fully stocked bread box with a toaster, a fully stocked cereal box with milk in the fridge, or even just free juice. Aside from low protein levels, this is a sustainable meal and is very healthy over all. You may be helping some people more by the fact that so many people today are obese. You may even be helping people in debt and that makes them loyal. That means, they are more tolerable of their minimum wage. This is one simple idea that I love to use and promote. Do not lump this idea with coffee and biscuits. Coffee actually makes for worse workers and biscuits are fattening and too easy to eat. Other things you can do for your minimum wage employees could also be along the line of giving them flexible working hours, providing discounts from your business (depending on what it is), or even allowing them to take care of their children on site (job permitting). Child care in all western worlds is enormously expensive (I have considered a child care business and may do one in the future), imagine taking that expense out of your employee.

A low minimum wage only effects people who work for bad businesses.
